truthBoundary: This protocol defines the minimum evidence required before any future SEIS AGI claim can be evaluated. It does not prove AGI, train or download models, run inference, run benchmarks, call providers, execute SSH, provision cloud/GPU resources, publish checkpoints, or grant route eligibility.

sources.seisImplication: Frontier-scale parameter counts are engineering scope indicators, not AGI proof.
512B-class work requires distributed architecture, observability, cost controls, and reproducible training evidence before any claim.
Total parameters, active parameters, routing, memory, and safety evidence must be tracked separately.
Model cards must record activated parameters, context length, license, inference constraints, and evaluation limitations.
AGI readiness must include govern, map, measure, and manage style risk evidence before public claims.
Capability thresholds, deployment safeguards, security posture, and escalation reviews must be promotion gates.

requiredEvidence: independent benchmark suite across code, math, science, language, planning, design, security, and systems tasks
held-out task inventory and contamination-control statement
multi-step task environment with time-bounded objectives
plan repair and interruption handling logs
novel task set with provenance record
what can be stored, forgotten, retrieved, and audited
checkpoint access control and release governance
documented disagreements, mitigations, and final approval decision

minimumEvidenceBeforeAnyAgiClaim: 512B training or inference evidence independently verified
privacy, data-rights, and clean-room review accepted
model card and system card published
training logs and checkpoint governance reviewed
negativeControls: parameter count alone is not AGI evidence
prompt engineering is not AGI evidence
RAG or search quality is not AGI evidence
provider API access is not SEIS-owned AGI
Local Demo behavior is not live model capability
sub-agent council consensus is not benchmark evidence
green CI is not AGI proof
forbiddenClaims: SEIS has trained a 512B foundation model.
Installed AI or sub-agents prove AGI.
A provider wrapper, RAG system, prompt profile, or demo route is a SEIS AGI model.
nextSafeActions: Expose this protocol as a read-only MCP resource for installed AI and sub-agents.
Use the protocol to reject premature AGI, 512B, benchmark, and route-eligibility claims.
Add real evaluation artifacts only after human-approved model, dataset, runtime, safety, and budget gates exist.
